_readme: This file holds all the editable text, links, and content for the site. To change something, edit the value after the colon (the part in quotes, or the number/true/false). Do not rename anything before a colon — the code looks for those exact names — and don't remove any commas, quotes, curly braces {} or square brackets [], or the file will stop working. Any key starting with an underscore, like this one, is just a note for humans and isn't read by the site; feel free to delete them, but leaving them in place won't cause any problems.

codeSnippet._comment: Powers the small 'typed code' animation. 'writes' is the list of languages it types out, one per line — add, remove, or reorder them freely. 'status' is the last line it types.

about._comment: The 'About' section. 'imagePath' is the photo shown next to the text — add the image to the project's images and put its path here. 'paragraphs' is the body text: one string per paragraph, add or remove as needed. 'facts' are the label/value rows below the paragraphs; each item needs a short 'label' and its 'value' — add or remove items freely.
about.sectionTitle: I like the whole path from blank file to shipped
paragraphs: I started with HTML and CSS, moved into JavaScript and React, then picked up Python and C/C++ to understand what happens underneath the browser. That mix means I can build an interface and also reason about the code that feeds it.

I care about pages that load quickly, work with a keyboard, and read well on a small screen. Outside of client work I write small tools for myself and read other people's code to learn how they solve problems.

skills._comment: The interactive language picker. 'endLabels' are the two captions shown at either end of the slider.
skills.sectionTitle: Six languages, from the browser to the machine
skills.sectionDescription: Most of my day is spent in the browser stack. Python and C round out the automation work and the parts that need to run close to the hardware. Pick a language to see how I use it.
skills._skillCardContentGuide: Each object in the list below is one language card. Fields: id (short, unique, lowercase — not shown on screen, just used internally); language (the big heading, e.g. 'JavaScript'); fileExtension (the small pill next to it, e.g. '.js'); color (a hex code like '#E0A800' used for that card's accent color); confidence (a number from 1 to 5 — how many bars are filled in); lineCount (how many lines the 'code' sample below produces — this must match or the line numbers won't line up); code (the snippet in the little code window, split into pieces — each piece has 'text', with \n marking where a new line starts, and 'className', which should be '' for plain text, 'text-sky-400' for keywords, 'text-amber-300' for function or class names, or 'text-emerald-400' for strings); useWith and builtWith (one sentence each, shown on the right of the card); workWith (the fileExtensions, like '.css', of related languages — these become the clickable pills that jump to that card). To add a language, copy one whole { ... } block below, including the comma before the next one, and edit every field.

projects._comment: The projects grid and its filter buttons.
projects.sectionDescription: A mix of client work, side projects, and coursework.
projects._filtersGuide: Each filter button needs a 'label' (the text on the button). The 'All' button has no 'languages' field and always shows every project. Every other button needs a 'languages' array — a project shows under that filter if any of its own 'language' values are in this list. Group languages together the way 'C / C++' does below if you want one button to match more than one language.
projects._projectListGuide: Each object below is one project card. Fields: name; description; language (an array of strings — use the exact spelling 'HTML', 'CSS', 'JS', 'JSX', 'Python', 'C', or 'C++' so the filters above match correctly); hasLive (true or false — whether to show a live-site link); liveUrl (only needed when hasLive is true); sourceUrl (link to the code); images (an array of image paths — leave it as [] to show a placeholder box instead of a photo). To add a project, copy one whole { ... } block below, including the comma before the next one, and edit every field.

projectList.name: Bitmap Image Viewer
projectList.description: A simple BMP image viewer written in C using SDL2. This project focuses on parsing and rendering BMP files with support for multiple formats and compression types.

projectList.name: LC-3 Virtual Machine (Python)
projectList.description: A simple LC-3 (Little Computer 3) virtual machine implemented in Python. This project emulates the LC-3 architecture, including registers, memory, instruction set, and trap routines.

projectList.name: PH Acquired Properties Scraper
projectList.description: Scrapes publicly listed acquired/foreclosed real estate from four Philippine government and bank sources, combines them into one normalized dataset, and optionally loads everything into MySQL.

projectList.name: TLS Analyzer
projectList.description: A from-scratch, live TLS handshake inspector — built to learn packet capture, protocol parsing, and systems programming from the wire up.

projectList.name: WinEventHook
projectList.description: A lightweight Windows console application written in C using the Win32 API. WinEventHook records and replays keyboard and mouse input using low-level Windows hooks and SendInput().

projectList.name: Todo App
projectList.description: A responsive todo app built with React and Tailwind CSS. Supports adding, completing, deleting, and filtering todos, a persistent light/dark theme, and drag-and-drop reordering using the native HTML5 Drag and Drop API.

projectList.name: Weather App
projectList.description: A weather app built with vanilla JavaScript and the Open-Meteo API. Features city search with debounced autocomplete, current conditions, hourly and 7-day forecasts, and switchable metric/imperial units, all in a responsive layout.

projectList.name: Order Summary Card
projectList.description: A small order summary card built as a Flexbox layout exercise. Uses Flexbox for centering and stacking the card contents, with hover states on the interactive elements.

projectList.name: Interactive Rating Component
projectList.description: An interactive rating card with a "Thank you" state after submitting. Uses visually restyled radio buttons for single-select ratings and JavaScript to switch between states.

projectList.name: Bento Grid
projectList.description: A responsive bento grid layout built with CSS Grid. Uses named grid areas and media queries to rearrange the boxes across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

projectList.name: Age Calculator App
projectList.description: An age calculator that takes a birth date and shows the age in years, months, and days. Includes form validation for empty, out-of-range, invalid, and future dates, with a responsive layout.

contact._comment: The closing section. 'email', 'github', and 'linkedin' show as contact links — 'github' and 'linkedin' should be full links starting with https://. 'formNote' is the small print shown under the message form.
contact.sectionDescription: Tell me what you're building and when you need it. I reply to every message within two working days.
contact.formNote: This opens a draft in your email app. Nothing is sent until you press send there.
